question: Why is Earth's gravity in metres per second squared, 9.81, so close to π squared, 9.87?
answer: Because the metre nearly was a pendulum. A pendulum whose single swing takes one second is g/π² metres long, and in 1791 the French Academy weighed it as the new unit. It chose instead a ten-millionth of the pole-to-equator arc, since gravity varies with latitude; that arc landed within 0.6% of the pendulum.
move: When two numbers match too well, look for a shared history before calling it luck.
ask: When two things match too neatly, do I look for a shared history before calling it luck?
source: Alder, The Measure of All Things, 2002
reference: Alder, The Measure of All Things: The Seven-Year Odyssey and Hidden Error That Transformed the World, Free Press, 2002
